how_to_read: A shift of one number between the two result sets is 'expected' when a rule below covers its board, model, cell and metric and its direction and size are inside the bounds; 'to be explained' when the item is a plausible cause and no study gives the size; 'unexplained' when no rule covers it. A must_not_move entry wins over every rule. Sizes: abs_k in K, rel_rise as a fraction of the baseline rise of the hottest point, rel as a fraction of the baseline value (counts). Status: 'quantified' = the bound is a number printed by a study; 'derived' = the bound is worked out from a printed number or is an engineering margin; 'to be explained' = no size known. Everything not measured here is left as 'to be explained' on purpose. Review: 'expected_out_of_range' is an alarm too (a defect on a board that an item reaches shows exactly so). Each bound is applied only to its unit: abs_k and rel_rise to temperatures, rel to unknown counts, abs_w (W) to the heat balance; the field checksums are not bounded. 'limits' (written by scripts/study_tighten_table.py from the reviewed run, 1.25 x the measured shift per board, model and cell, floors 0.05 K, 0.1 % of a count, 1e-9 W, 1 % of a time to 63 %) replace the general bound, which stays as the hypothesis of the documents.
